title:
PROBABILITY,
(MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE EVENTS)
objective: LO: I can identify mutually exclusive events and use the addition rule for probability.

content.text: Mutually exclusive events cannot happen at the same time. If one occurs, the other cannot occur.
Addition rule: If A and B are mutually exclusive, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

examples.expr: Rolling a 3 and rolling a 5 on one die: mutually exclusive
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) when mutually exclusive
All probabilities in a sample space sum to 1
Drawing a red card and a king are mutually exclusive
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) always

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Mutually exclusive events have no overlap: P(A and B) = 0. So P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
key_idea.caption: Only when A and B cannot happen together

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – identifying mutually exclusive
modelled_examples.question: A die is rolled. Are 'rolling a 2' and 'rolling an even number' mutually exclusive?
steps: Rolling a 2 IS an even number
Both can happen on the same roll
modelled_examples.explanation: 2 is contained within the set of even numbers.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – addition rule
modelled_examples.question: P(red) = 0.3, P(blue) = 0.45. If colours are mutually exclusive, find P(red or blue).
modelled_examples.explanation: Simply add the probabilities when events cannot overlap.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – finding a missing probability
modelled_examples.question: A spinner has P(red) = 0.2, P(blue) = 0.35, P(green) = 0.15. Find P(yellow).
modelled_examples.explanation: The sample space is exhaustive so all probabilities total 1.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – or probability from a table
modelled_examples.question: A bag: 5 red, 3 blue, 2 green (total 10). Find P(red or green).
steps: Red and green are mutually exclusive (a ball is one colour)
modelled_examples.explanation: Each ball is only one colour, so colours are mutually exclusive.

practice.instruction: State whether each pair is mutually exclusive (Yes/No).

practice.heading: Finding missing probabilities
practice.instruction: All outcomes are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
